label: Luke 23:1
text: The whole company of them rose up and brought him before Pilate.

label: Luke 23:2
text: They began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man perverting the nation, forbidding paying taxes to Caesar, and saying that he himself is Christ, a king.”

label: Luke 23:3
text:
Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
He answered him,
“So you say.”

label: Luke 23:4
text: Pilate said to the chief priests and the multitudes, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”

label: Luke 23:5
text: But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee even to this place.”

label: Luke 23:6
text: But when Pilate heard Galilee mentioned, he asked if the man was a Galilean.

label: Luke 23:7
text: When he found out that he was in Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem during those days.

label: Luke 23:8
text: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly glad, for he had wanted to see him for a long time, because he had heard many things about him. He hoped to see some miracle done by him.

label: Luke 23:9
text: He questioned him with many words, but he gave no answers.

label: Luke 23:10
text: The chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.

label: Luke 23:11
text: Herod with his soldiers humiliated him and mocked him. Dressing him in luxurious clothing, they sent him back to Pilate.

label: Luke 23:12
text: Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day, for before that they were enemies with each other.

label: Luke 23:13
text: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,

label: Luke 23:14
text: and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one that perverts the people, and behold, having examined him before you, I found no basis for a charge against this man concerning those things of which you accuse him.

label: Luke 23:15
text: Neither has Herod, for I sent you to him, and see, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.

label: Luke 23:16
text: I will therefore chastise him and release him.”

label: Luke 23:17
text: Now he had to release one prisoner to them at the feast.

variants.reading: the whole verse ('Now he had to release one prisoner to them at the feast.') omitted
variants.note: Missing from Papyrus 75, Codex Alexandrinus, Codex Vaticanus and others; present in Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Washingtonianus, Family 1 and Family 13. The verse parallels Matthew 27:15 and Mark 15:6 and is suspected of assimilation into Luke (Wikipedia, List of omitted Bible verses, Luke 23:17).
Codex Sinaiticus carries Luke 23:17 (Wikipedia, List of omitted Bible verses).

label: Luke 23:18
text: But they all cried out together, saying, “Away with this man! Release to us Barabbas!”—

label: Luke 23:19
text: one who was thrown into prison for a certain revolt in the city, and for murder.

label: Luke 23:20
text: Then Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus,

label: Luke 23:21
text: but they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify him!”

label: Luke 23:22
text: He said to them the third time, “Why? What evil has this man done? I have found no capital crime in him. I will therefore chastise him and release him.”

label: Luke 23:23
text: But they were urgent with loud voices, asking that he might be crucified. Their voices and the voices of the chief priests prevailed.

label: Luke 23:24
text: Pilate decreed that what they asked for should be done.

label: Luke 23:25
text: He released him who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, for whom they asked, but he delivered Jesus up to their will.

label: Luke 23:26
text: When they led him away, they grabbed one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid on him the cross, to carry it after Jesus.

label: Luke 23:27
text: A great multitude of the people followed him, including women who also mourned and lamented him.

label: Luke 23:28
text:
But Jesus, turning to them, said,
“Daughters of Jerusalem, don’t weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.

label: Luke 23:29
text: For behold, the days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, the wombs that never bore, and the breasts that never nursed.’

label: Luke 23:30
text: Then they will begin to tell the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and tell the hills, ‘Cover us.’

label: Luke 23:31
text: For if they do these things in the green tree, what will be done in the dry?”

label: Luke 23:32
text: There were also others, two criminals, led with him to be put to death.

label: Luke 23:33
text: When they came to the place that is called The Skull, they crucified him there with the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.

label: Luke 23:34
text:
Jesus said,
“Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.

variants.reading: the sentence 'Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.' omitted
variants.note: Omitted in P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, D*, W, Theta and other early witnesses; included in the majority text. Ehrman argues the words were omitted by some scribes because of anti-Judaic sentiment around the second century (Wikipedia, Papyrus 75; Sayings of Jesus on the cross).

label: Luke 23:35
text: The people stood watching. The rulers with them also scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen one!”

label: Luke 23:36
text: The soldiers also mocked him, coming to him and offering him vinegar,

label: Luke 23:37
text: and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!”

label: Luke 23:38
text: An inscription was also written over him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

variants.reading: 'in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew' absent: 'There was also an inscription above him: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.'
variants.note: Alexandrian text-type (Westcott and Hort 1881, NA27/UBS4); the Byzantine text carries the trilingual detail (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:38).

label: Luke 23:39
text: One of the criminals who was hanged insulted him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!”

variants.reading: 'Are you not the Christ? Save yourself and us!' (Alexandrian) against 'If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!' (Byzantine)
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:39.

label: Luke 23:40
text: But the other answered, and rebuking him said, “Don’t you even fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?

label: Luke 23:41
text: And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward for our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong.”

label: Luke 23:42
text: He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”

variants.reading: 'And he said: Jesus, remember me' (Alexandrian) against 'And he said to Jesus: Remember me, Lord' (Byzantine)
variants.note: Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:42.

label: Luke 23:43
text:
Jesus said to him,
“Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”

label: Luke 23:44
text: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

label: Luke 23:45
text: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.

variants.reading: 'the sun's light failed' (tou heliou eklipontos; Alexandrian) against 'and the sun was darkened' (Byzantine)
variants.note: Alexandrian text-type (Westcott and Hort 1881, NA27/UBS4, Nestle 1904); the Byzantine text reads 'and the sun was darkened', which the WEB follows (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:45).

label: Luke 23:46
text:
Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said,
“Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” Having said this, he breathed his last.

label: Luke 23:47
text: When the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this was a righteous man.”

label: Luke 23:48
text: All the multitudes that came together to see this, when they saw the things that were done, returned home beating their breasts.

label: Luke 23:49
text: All his acquaintances, and the women who followed with him from Galilee, stood at a distance, watching these things.

label: Luke 23:50
text: Behold, a man named Joseph, who was a member of the council, a good and righteous man

label: Luke 23:51
text: (he had not consented to their counsel and deed), from Arimathaea, a city of the Jews, who was also waiting for God’s Kingdom:

label: Luke 23:52
text: this man went to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.

label: Luke 23:53
text: He took it down, and wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb that was cut in stone, where no one had ever been laid.

label: Luke 23:54
text: It was the day of the Preparation, and the Sabbath was drawing near.

label: Luke 23:55
text: The women, who had come with him out of Galilee, followed after, and saw the tomb, and how his body was laid.

label: Luke 23:56
text: They returned, and prepared spices and ointments. On the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.

label: Hosea 10:8 ('they will say to the mountains, Cover us!')
author: Hosea (traditional attribution)

label: Psalm 31:5 ('into your hand I commend my spirit')
author: David (traditional attribution)

label: The charges before Pilate: perverting the nation, forbidding tribute to Caesar
statement: The chief priests accused Jesus before Pilate of perverting the nation, forbidding the payment of tribute to Caesar, and claiming to be Christ, a king.
note: Luke's charge list is unique: Matthew 27:11 and Mark 15:2 record only the 'King of the Jews' charge.

label: Pilate declares Jesus innocent three times
statement: Pilate told the chief priests and the crowd that he found no basis for a capital charge against Jesus, and that Herod found nothing worthy of death either.
note: Luke states the innocence verdict three times (23:4, 14-15, 22); Matthew instead has Pilate's wife's dream and the hand-washing (27:19, 24).

label: Galilee was under Herod Antipas's jurisdiction
statement: When Pilate heard that Jesus was a Galilean, Galilee was under Herod Antipas's jurisdiction, so the case fell outside Pilate's own province.
note: Luke alone reports the jurisdictional reasoning; Josephus assigns Perea and Galilee to Antipas as tetrarch.

label: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Antipas, who was in Jerusalem
statement: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod Antipas, who was in Jerusalem during those days.
note: Luke only. Antipas's presence in Jerusalem fits the Passover pilgrimage season.

label: Herod and his soldiers mocked Jesus and dressed him in splendid clothing
statement: Herod with his soldiers treated Jesus with contempt and mocked him; dressing him in splendid clothing, they sent him back to Pilate.
note: The mockery is by Herod and his soldiers (Luke only); in Matthew 27:27-31 and Mark 15:16-20 it is Pilate's soldiers, and Mark's robe is purple.

label: Herod and Pilate became friends that day
statement: Herod and Pilate, previously at enmity with each other, became friends with each other that very day.
note: Luke only. The Pontius Pilate article reports that Daniel Schwartz takes both the difficult relationship and its mending as potentially historical.

label: Pilate proposed to chastise Jesus and release him
statement: Pilate proposed to chastise (paideusas) Jesus and then release him, as a compromise short of crucifixion.
note: In Matthew 27:26 and Mark 15:15 the scourging is actually carried out before the release/crucifixion; Luke frames chastisement as Pilate's repeated proposal.

label: The lamenting women of Jerusalem followed him
statement: A great multitude of the people followed Jesus, including women of Jerusalem who mourned and lamented him, and he turned and addressed them.
note: Luke alone gives the lamenting women and the address to the 'daughters of Jerusalem' (23:27-31).

label: Days are coming: blessed are the barren, the mountains fall on us
statement: Jesus warned the women that days were coming when they would say 'blessed are the barren' and call on the mountains to fall and the hills to cover them, closing with the green-tree proverb.
note: Verse 30 echoes Hosea 10:8. A prediction: evidence can attest the destruction of 70 CE that the warning points to, not that it was predicted.

label: 'Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing'
statement: Jesus said, 'Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing.'
note: Textually uncertain: the sentence is omitted in P75, Sinaiticus and Vaticanus and other early witnesses, and is included in the majority text (see the variants on passage:lk-23-34).

label: The soldiers mocked him and offered sour wine
statement: The soldiers came to Jesus and mocked him, offering him vinegar and saying, 'If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.'
note: Luke: soldiers offer sour wine during the mockery; Matthew 27:48 and Mark 15:36 have sour wine on a sponge raised on a reed at the moment of the death cry.

label: The inscription in Greek, Latin and Hebrew letters
statement: An inscription was written over him in letters of Greek, Latin and Hebrew: 'THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.'
note: The trilingual detail is the Byzantine reading; the Alexandrian text reads only 'There was also an inscription above him' (Wikipedia, Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke, Luke 23:38). The WEB follows the Byzantine text here.

label: The two criminals: one blasphemed, one asked to be remembered
statement: One criminal insulted Jesus; the other rebuked him, confessed his own guilt, said Jesus had done nothing wrong, and asked, 'Jesus, remember me when you come into your Kingdom'; Jesus answered, 'today you will be with me in Paradise'.
note: Matthew 27:44 and Mark 15:32 have both criminals reviling Jesus; Luke alone splits them and records the exchange. Luke 23:42 Alexandrian reads 'Jesus, remember me'; Byzantine 'Remember me, Lord'.

label: The sun's light failed
statement: The sun's light failed (Luke's distinctive wording, tou heliou eklipontos in the Alexandrian text; the Byzantine text and WEB read 'the sun was darkened').
note: Luke's verb ekleipo is the word for eclipse and invited eclipse readings of the darkness (Thallus, Phlegon); see the complicates edge from the eclipse-impossible observation.

label: 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit'
statement: Jesus cried with a loud voice, 'Father, into your hands I commit my spirit', and died.
note: The final cry differs: Matthew 27:46 and Mark 15:34 quote Psalm 22:1 ('My God, my God, why have you forsaken me'); Luke quotes Psalm 31:5.

label: The centurion: 'Certainly this was a righteous man'
statement: When the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God and said, 'Certainly this was a righteous man.'
note: Matthew 27:54 and Mark 15:39 record the centurion saying 'truly this was the Son of God'; Luke records 'righteous/innocent'.

label: Joseph of Arimathea had not consented to their counsel
statement: Joseph, a member of the council from the Jewish city of Arimathea, was a good and righteous man who had not consented to their counsel and deed, and was waiting for God's Kingdom.
note: Luke alone: the non-consent to the council's deed and the waiting for the Kingdom; Mark 15:43 makes him a prominent bouleutes.

label: The women prepared spices and rested on the Sabbath
statement: The women returned from the tomb and prepared spices and ointments, and on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
note: Mark 16:1 has the women buy spices after the Sabbath; Luke has them prepare spices before it and rest on the Sabbath itself.
